quest.title: Tower of Inversion
quest.description: You find a mysterious summons coming from the high tower...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Vlaicu
dialogues.text: There've been Wild Hunt sightings here. We're on the case, but you should keep your distance for your own safety.

response.speaker: Vlaicu
response.text: Lots of adventurers say that with confidence... Still, if danger comes up, please go straight to a Lightkeeper patrolling nearby.

talks.objective: Head to the Pillar of Embla

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. You've returned.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Apologies for the long wait, Miss Alia. We ran into some monsters on the way back.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: It's alright. To me, that was barely a blink of an eye.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Ah, my apologies. That was a slip of the tongue...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Hehe. The way you tense up like that does remind me a little of Solovei. No wonder that nightingale chose to stay by your side.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know about Aedon, too? Wait, is he also a bird from five hundred years ago? There's no way, right?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Quite perceptive, Paimon. Your guess is correct.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Paimon had a feeling Aedon was special! You can tell right away he's not just any messenger bird!

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: He was once Solovei's nightingale, following him from their homeland to this bitter frontier.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Later, when Solovei resolved to cast aside the Nightingale family name, he meant to drive the bird away. I couldn't let it end up homeless, so I took it in.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: I could never have foreseen that this small act would see it pulled into the Sampo Mill and carried across five hundred years, thus taking the form you see now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "Sampo Mill"...?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Considering you first took me for a fae, it's not surprising that the term is unfamiliar to you. So much time has passed, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: But you will have to face the "Professor" yourselves soon, won't you?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: While we still have a moment, I believe it is necessary to tell you the true history — the truth of the serpent's first death.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: For just as I am no fae worthy of worship, this tower you call the Pillar of Embla is no divine miracle.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: On the contrary... This is the place where I slew that serpent for the first time — yet failed to consign him to hell for good.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: At that time, the "Professor" erected a tower here — one that reached toward the very heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: He sought to use the Sampo Mill to siphon the land's power and, through that tower, ascend to the "Elysium" he believed lay beyond the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Had his scheme succeeded, all of Nod-Krai — its soil and every living being upon it — would have become fuel for his ascent.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: We did all we could to stop him, but we were far too weak. By the time we reached this place, he was but one step shy of his goal...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: With no other recourse, I cast myself into the Sampo Mill and used my own flesh and blood to ignite it, thwarting that serpent's plot.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Heh... thinking back on it now, that was the first — and the last — time I ever felt grateful for the bloodline I was born with.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: As I've said before, I am no more than a mortal. It was by a twist of fate alone that I came to linger in the seam between time and space.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Miss Alia...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: As for the serpent's second death... as Solovei's successor, you should know that story even better than I.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Yes. It is said that five hundred years ago, the Moonchanter of that era entrusted the sacred blade to the Torchforger, and together with many others, they drove the fiend and his followers back to Kipumaki Cliff...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: In the end, the Moonchanter and the Torchforger sealed the monster with their own hands.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Twice shall that undying serpent rise again..."

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: And now we stand at the third and final time — the moment when that serpent must be buried for good.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: "Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down... And at last shall he be laid to rest by the heroes of the sublunary sphere..."

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Rest assured, Miss Alia. This time, we will put him down for good. We will not allow past tragedies to repeat themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we'll help too!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Really? But you two...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait — do you mean that once you get the Silver Lampwick from Miss Alia, you won't need our help anymore, and we should just part ways?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Paimon never would've thought you were such a cold person, Illuga...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: I—I'm sorry, I didn't mean to distance myself. It's just...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Pfft— alright, alright, we know you worry about us. But seriously, you don't have to. You've seen for yourself what {NICKNAME} is capable of on the road, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can leave your back to me.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: #{NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Hehe, with such "the heroes of the sublunary sphere" to rely on, I suppose it's time I made up my mind as well.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Once I hand you the Silver Lampwick, the barriers in this region will all collapse. When that happens, the Abyss will reclaim this place.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: The "Professor" will surely return. Reaching that "Elysium" beyond the firmament through this tower was his life's obsession. Even in death, that fixation has never faded.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: I will use everything I have to hold him here. While I do, you must find a way to end him for good.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: The one who asked you to gather the relics must already have a plan in place. You'd do well to follow his instructions.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: But Miss Alia... If you do that, then you...

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Don't worry. No one shall send me packing from this world until that wretched serpent is laid to rest for good.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: ...There's an old saying about Winter Iceleas. I don't know if it still survives in your era: "Though the flower may fail, the leaves will keep their promise."

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Sorry, I've never heard it...

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Is that so? A pity, but it doesn't matter. All you need to understand is this — what I do now is simply a promise I must uphold.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Miss Alia... I'll keep my promise too. I swore to you — no matter what happens, I will... I will put an end to the "Professor"!

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Not "you," but "all of you." No one should walk their path alone, Illuga... and no one should march alone toward death.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't forget that we're here, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! And it's not just us — there are tons and tons of Lightkeepers who have your back! We'll be totally fine!

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: ...There's no time left. I must send you off now.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "Don't look back. Run, children, run."

choices.text: Like I'd ever sit back and let villains run wild.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Honestly, you should look into it — there's not a single bad guy out there who hears our names and doesn't start shaking in their boots!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even those Abyss monsters without legs would be shaking all over! Anyway, there's no way we'd just ignore something evil.

dialogues.text: Are you hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're fine. Thanks for stepping in to help!
I'm glad to hear that. These pitch-black impurities are far more dangerous than they look. Any wounds they inflict can have serious consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Abyss is nothing I can't handle.
Strong as you may be, it's my duty as a Lightkeeper to remind you not to let your guard down.
And that strange little... Jack Frost you're carrying doesn't appear suited for combat either...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's not a Jack Frost! But at least she wasn't mistaken for a specter this time... Ugh. Not the point! Paimon's {NICKNAME}'s guide, thank you very much!
Ah, my apologies... I assure you, I meant no offense. So you're a guide...

Guiding outlanders like you two was originally one of our responsibilities as well. It's just that the recent surge in Wild Hunt activity has made things... difficult. Hah... let's set that aside for now.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'm Illuga, captain of the Lightkeepers' investigation squad, the Nightmare Orioles. It's a pleasure to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's Paimon and {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers. We noticed Abyssal corruption here, so we came over to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: You knowingly stepped into an area tainted by the Abyss... That's... well, in any case, this place is far too dangerous. I should get you both back down first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... But what are you doing here? You don't have to patrol a place this dangerous, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Honestly... This isn't the best look for me, but I came here in search of a sacred relic. I ended up spending too much time clearing out the monsters in the area, so I've made almost no progress...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: And I've dragged the two of you into danger on top of that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's nothing. These little scrapes don't even make it into our adventure log!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But a relic, huh... Would it have anything to do with that strange voice we heard earlier? Something about "the heroes of the sublunary sphere"...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Oh? You heard that fae's call as well? Then it seems she's acknowledged you two...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait what? What fae?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Well... I should probably start from the beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: The relic we're searching for is the Silver Lampwick, one of three sacred artifacts — <color=#FF9999FF>the sword, the lamp, and the mirror</color> — used by the Torchforger five hundred years ago to defeat the fiend of Kipumaki Cliff.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: It can deploy a barrier capable of resisting the Wild Hunt. With the Wild Hunt resurfacing at Kipumaki Cliff, the old man sent us out to recover it.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: It is said that after the calamity was quelled, the Torchforger entrusted the relic to Alia, the fae who guards the Pillar of Embla.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... How are we supposed to meet her, then? This place doesn't exactly look like somewhere a fae would live...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Following the kuuvahki's guiding light should lead you to her. "Should" being the operative term. Right now, that guide is flickering...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'd say it's half the Abyssal corruption, and half her intention. She's using kuuvahki to obscure that which is truly important... including her own presence.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: As such, we'll likely need the power of a <color=#00E1FFFF>Barrier Core</color> to disperse the corruption and restore the barriers in this area. Once the barrier reforms, our now-hidden guide should reveal itself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll help you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We're great at tracking things down, and if the Abyss is to blame, there's no way we're turning a blind eye.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: But danger lurks behind every corner here, and the terrain is treacherous. Why don't you two wait somewhere safe while I—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #No way! Hey, seriously, aren't you underestimating {NICKNAME} just a little?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You saw {M#him}{F#her} in action just now — pretty impressive, right? Honestly... {M#he}{F#she} might even be stronger than you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And besides, {M#he's}{F#she's} got Paimon, the ever-reliable guide! Tricky terrain? Puh-lease. Paimon can fly!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I don't mean to belittle you. But you're ordinary people who were kind enough to help us out. If something happened to you because of all this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Just leave it to us. We won't let you down!

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Alright, alright. Then I'll be counting on you. But please, be careful. I'll do everything I can to keep you safe as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We will. Heh, if anything, you should be the one watching your step.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Thanks. That said... I also have a companion who can fly. Come on, Aedon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! He's all gold and shiny, just like a pile of Mora!

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Let's start with the barrier core nearby. Once we're close, we just need to channel the kuuvahki into it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?! But that thing's floating in midair! Paimon can get there just fine, but you two...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: No worries. Come with me, I'll show you just what Aedon can do.

choices.text: I might get annoyed if you don't stop fussing.

talks.objective: Investigate the core shrouded in Abyssal energy

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Paimon does feel a teeny-tiny bit of kuuvahki in it, but it's all covered in Abyssal goop. It can't function at all like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, could you try purifying it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know — the move that makes all the Abyss corruption go fwoosh and disappear.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Look out!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'll hold them off! Get out of here as quickly as you can, now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no way I'm running away!
Heroes of the sublunary sphere... clear the Abyssal energy from the core so I can lend you my aid!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's do as she says!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... hello? Paimon doesn't know who you are, but we gotta clear that Abyssal energy from the core, right?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Wait, what are you doing?

talks.objective: Follow Illuga to activate the barrier core

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Are you hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're fine. Thanks for stepping in to help!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'm glad to hear that. These pitch-black impurities are far more dangerous than they look. Any wounds they inflict can have serious consequences.

choices.text: The Abyss is nothing I can't handle.

response.text: Strong as you may be, it's my duty as a Lightkeeper to remind you not to let your guard down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of Lightkeepers... oh! You're Illuga, right? The old man back in Piramida told us about you, and we even saw you there!

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: ...Oh? Now that you mention it, I did catch sight of a rather unusual little Jack Frost in the crowd.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's not a Jack Frost! But at least she wasn't mistaken for a specter this time... Ugh. Not the point! Paimon's {NICKNAME}'s guide, thank you very much!

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: In any case, your guess is correct. I'm Illuga, captain of the Lightkeepers' investigation squad, the Nightmare Orioles. It's a pleasure to meet you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}. We're here on a commission — and actually, that commission has something to do with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! An old Lightkeeper asked us to...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You briefly explain how you took on a sudden commission in Piramida and came to the Pillar of Embla in search of the Silver Lampwick...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: I see... He can't keep from worrying about me, huh? Can't blame him, though.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Honestly... This isn't the best look for me, but I came here looking for the Silver Lampwick as well. I ended up spending too much time clearing out the monsters in the area, so I've made almost no progress...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: And I've dragged the two of you into danger on top of that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, it's nothing. These little scrapes don't even make it into our adventure log!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, we never got to ask properly... We have to find the fae named Alia to get the Silver Lampwick, right? So... where exactly are we supposed to look for her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! And that voice we heard earlier... was that her?

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: So you heard it too... Yes, I believe that was her guiding us.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Following the kuuvahki's guiding light should lead you to her. "Should" being the operative term. Right now, that guide is flickering...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm! We've accepted the commission, after all! And since the Abyss is the cause of all this, there's no way we're just gonna ignore it!

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: No worries. Come with me, I'll show you just what Aedon can do.

choices.text: I might get annoyed if you don't stop fussing.
I remember you. Back in Piramida...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! You're the one that old man mentioned! We saw you there earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'll stay here to keep channeling energy into the barrier core. May I entrust the other side to you two? Aedon will lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Aedon's helping out, we'll be totally fine! You can leave it to us.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Thank you. That means we'll be apart for a bit. Stay safe, you two!

talks.objective: Activate the barrier core on the other side

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Where... where are we? What is this place? Everything around us looks completely different...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon... Paimon thinks she saw a bunch of weird stuff just now... and now her head's all spinny...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, me too...
Travelers flowing along the river of time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, who are you!? When did you get here!?
Hmm? Well, I heard someone calling my name... Was that not you?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Calling your name... Ah! So you must be Miss Alia — the fae who guards the Silver Lampwick here at the Pillar of Embla!

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Relic? Fae? Heh... So that's what I've become in your time? A legend far removed from the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: I'm no fae. I'm... just an ordinary human. The Silver Lampwick is indeed here, but where did you...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...No, let me ask it this way. Since you know of the Lampwick, you must have heard the name Solovei as well. In your time... which age does he belong to?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Do you mean the Torchforger? He founded the Lightkeepers about... five hundred years ago now.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...Five hundred years... So it's already been that long...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, so you're not a fae? Then... hang on... are you seriously over five hundred years old!?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: The legends may have twisted parts of the truth, but if you were the Torchforger's ally, and you can wield kuuvahki to guard the relic here... Miss Alia, you've clearly gone far beyond what ordinary mortals can reach.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...That's a long story. And right now, there are things far more important than my age.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: If you've come seeking the Silver Lampwick, then that means the "Professor" has slipped free again. Just as the prophecy warned... Solovei's seal was never going to hold him forever.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: By the "Professor," do you mean the fiend who was sealed within Kipumaki Cliff five hundred years ago by the Torchforger and the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: The prophecy says this: "Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down..." Serpent, fiend, or "Professor" — no matter the title, he's earned every bit of his infamy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It says he'll be struck down a third time, then?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Yes. Though rather than a prophecy destined to happen... I would say this was more like an earnest plea.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: After all, the one who gave that prophecy was just like me — she was someone from the past. When it comes to future disasters, there's so little we can do...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Our future became your present. And your future... It can only be shaped by those who live in the present.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Forgive the interruption... Three years ago, some senior Ratniki and I went to investigate a disturbance in the seal. But...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: We were hit by an ambush none of us expected... Our losses were severe, and the mission had to be called off.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: After that, the old man decided we weren't yet ready to solve the problem once and for all. He set up observation posts around the area, declaring it off-limits.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I know he intended to buy time, gather strength, and look for a way to turn the tide. But... still...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I shouldn't question his judgment, yet I can't help wondering — isn't this situation... the result of negligence on our part?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: We hesitated and dallied... and now, the great evil eye and countless monsters have come spilling out beyond the cordoned zone. Just thinking about the nightmare from three years ago being poured out over this land again... I just can't stand it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Illuga...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: #...Apologies, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Miss Alia. I lost my composure just now. Sorry about that.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: I don't know all the details of which you speak, but... a dulled blade must sometimes be honed before it can cut true again. That kind of sharpening is never wasted effort.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Besides, surely the world five hundred years on isn't so small that all its burdens must be piled onto the shoulders of a single child.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Ch—Child? You mean me? But I'm not a child anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Well, think about it. Strictly speaking, I'm a few centuries older than you. How could you not be a child in my eyes? Compared to me, you're all pretty much children.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon maybe, sure... but why am I a child too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What's with that tone? Aren't you happy to be called a child alongside Paimon? Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon does think Miss Alia has a point. This isn't something you should have to carry on your own. It's... It's on all of us!

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: If we're assigning blame, then I deserve it more than anyone here. Back then, I failed to truly destroy the "Professor"...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: And since then, I've wasted away in this stagnant prison of time. Even now, I cannot give you the Silver Lampwick you came for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miss Alia, don't say that... Wait. Does that mean the Silver Lampwick isn't actually with you?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: How should I put this... it both is and isn't. In your present, this tower has been deeply corrupted. This prevents me from freely using my power to reach the Silver Lampwick.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if we clear the corruption from the tower?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: That would be ideal. The tower's presence allows the kuuvahki here to remain in its purest form — you've already seen the creatures born from its influence.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: If the moon has blessed you, you may be able to use that same power to cleanse the filth clinging to the tower and restore its purity.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Once you've cleared the corruption and the strength I've lost gathers at the tower's peak once more... Come find me then.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Umm... Thank you for your guidance, Miss Alia. And... please don't blame yourself too much. I—

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: I know what you want to say. And if you're willing to forgive me, don't be so harsh on yourself, either.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: The past is beyond change. But the world of the living still has a future, and I'm entrusting that future to you.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...All right. It's time I sent you back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Where... where are we? What is this place? Everything around us looks completely different...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon... Paimon thinks she saw a bunch of weird stuff just now... and now her head's all spinny...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, me too...
Travelers flowing along the river of time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, who are you!? When did you get here!?
Hmm? Well, I heard someone calling my name... Was that not you?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Calling your name... Ah! So you must be Miss Alia — the fae who guards the Silver Lampwick here at the Pillar of Embla!

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Relic? Fae? Heh... So that's what I've become in your time? A legend far removed from the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: I'm no fae. I'm... just an ordinary human. The Silver Lampwick is indeed here, but where did you...

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...No, let me ask it this way. Since you know of the Lampwick, you must have heard the name Solovei as well. In your time... which age does he belong to?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Do you mean the Torchforger? He founded the Lightkeepers about... five hundred years ago now.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...Five hundred years... So it's already been that long...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—Wait, so you're not a fae? Then... hang on... are you seriously over five hundred years old!?

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: The legends may have twisted parts of the truth, but if you were the Torchforger's ally, and you can wield kuuvahki to guard the relic here... Miss Alia, you've clearly gone far beyond what ordinary mortals can reach.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: ...That's a long story. And right now, there are things far more important than my age.

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: If you've come seeking the Silver Lampwick, then that means the "Professor" has slipped free again. Just as the prophecy warned... Solovei's seal was never going to hold him forever.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: By the "Professor," do you mean the fiend who was sealed within Kipumaki Cliff five hundred years ago by the Torchforger and the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions?

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: The prophecy says this: "Twice shall that undying serpent rise again, but thrice shall he be struck down..." Serpent, fiend, or "Professor" — no matter the title, he's earned every bit of his infamy.

choices.text: It says he'll be struck down a third time, then?

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Yes. Though rather than a prophecy destined to happen... I would say this was more like an earnest plea.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: After all, oracle or no, she is just like me — a person from the past. When it comes to future disasters, there's so little we can do...

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Our future became your present. And your future... It can only be shaped by those who live in the present.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Forgive the interruption... Three years ago, some senior Ratniki and I went to investigate a disturbance in the seal. But...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: We were hit by an ambush none of us expected... Our losses were severe, and the mission had to be called off.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: After that, the old man decided we weren't yet ready to solve the problem once and for all. He set up observation posts around the area, declaring it off-limits.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: I know he intended to buy time, gather strength, and look for a way to turn the tide. But... still...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: I shouldn't question his judgment, yet I can't help wondering — isn't this situation... the result of negligence on our part?

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: We hesitated and dallied... and now, the great evil eye and countless monsters have come spilling out beyond the cordoned zone. Just thinking about the nightmare from three years ago being poured out over this land again... I just can't stand it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Illuga...

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: #...Apologies, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Miss Alia. I lost my composure just now. Sorry about that.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: I don't know all the details of which you speak, but... a dulled blade must sometimes be honed before it can cut true again. That kind of sharpening is never wasted effort.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Besides, surely the world five hundred years on isn't so small that all its burdens must be piled onto the shoulders of a single child.

response.speaker: Illuga
response.text: Ch—Child? You mean me? But I'm not a child anymore.

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Well, think about it. Strictly speaking, I'm a few centuries older than you. How could you not be a child in my eyes? Compared to me, you're all pretty much children.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon maybe, sure... but why am I a child too?

choices.text: I remember Aila saying something similar as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! We heard something like that from Aila back when we were in the Frostmoon Scions' sanctum with Verna...

response.speaker: Alia
response.text: Ah, so you've met Aila too... what a curious twist of fate. But again, hers is less a prophecy that's bound to happen... and more a plea for it to happen.

talks.objective: Cleanse the corruption throughout the area and restore the barrier core

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'll leave the barrier core over there in your care. Aedon, make sure you keep them safe and sound.

talks.objective: Head to the top of the tower
Head to the top of the tower

dialogues.text: Watch out!
I'll hold them off! Get out of here as quickly as you can, now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no way I'm running away!

dialogues.speaker: Alia
dialogues.text: Heroes of the sublunary sphere... clear the Abyssal energy from the core so I can lend you my aid!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's do as she says!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... hello? Paimon doesn't know who you are, but we gotta clear that Abyssal energy from the core, right?
Wait, what are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh... The Pillar of Embla's totally overrun by the Abyss... Paimon sure hopes Miss Alia's okay...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We just have to trust her and focus on what we can do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Yeah! We gotta keep it together, especially at times like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where next, Illuga? You know the situation best, so we'll follow your lead.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: First, I need to return to Piramida and hold an oath-taking ceremony with my squad. After that, we'll move to Cliffwatch Camp at the base of Kipumaki Cliff to prepare for the upcoming operation.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: As I mentioned, that area is considered extremely dangerous, a forbidden zone. What awaits us there will be a tough fight and dangers beyond imagination...

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: You two aren't Lightkeepers, so technically, I don't have the authority to command you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Given the situation, why not count us in?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon agrees! We've got some experience too, y'know! And for big operations like this, it's definitely better to follow orders than go it alone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lead us to victory, Captain!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Thank you... Hearing that gives me more courage, even in the face of our enemies, than you know.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I hereby officially invite you to join my Investigation Squad, the Nightmare Orioles.

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'll guide you, protect you, and uphold my promise to Miss Alia.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll protect you too — and the rest of your team! Let's stand together and see this through!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: That we will!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Since you're officially part of my squad now, how about we head to Piramida together for the oath-taking? I bet you haven't even seen our headquarters yet, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oath-taking, huh... sounds amazing! Count us in!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Still, this was a sudden development. So, if you need to make any preparations, use what time remains to us. A tough battle awaits, so there's no such thing as "too prepared."

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: I'll stick to the original plan and head for Cliffwatch Camp first. I'll wait for you there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it! We'll be there as soon as possible!

dialogues.speaker: Illuga
dialogues.text: Take care until then!
